title: Donald Trump Attended Fordham for Two Years Before Transferring to Penn
description_short: Trump attended Fordham’s Bronx campus for two years, then transferred to Penn; Fordham’s 1965 yearbook lists him as a freshman and squash-team member.
description_medium: Fordham’s student newspaper reported, based on alumni interviews, that Trump commuted to its Bronx campus for two years before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania. The article also cites Fordham’s 1965 Maroon yearbook listing him as a freshman on the squash team. This supports attendance by 1965, but not the timeline’s exact July 1, 1964 enrollment date.
description_long: A 2024 Fordham Ram report based on interviews with former classmates says Donald Trump attended Fordham’s Rose Hill campus in the Bronx for two years before transferring to the University of Pennsylvania. The article describes him as a commuting student from Queens and says he later completed his degree at Penn in 1968. It cites Fordham’s 1965 Maroon yearbook, which lists Trump as a freshman and member of the squash team, alongside alumni recollections of their commutes and student life. These sources support the broad educational chronology and his presence at Fordham by 1965. They do not establish July 1, 1964 as an exact enrollment date. The record’s separate allegation that his sister completed homework for him is not supported by these sources and is omitted. The narrower factual draft is biographical context; it does not document a public act, policy decision, or harm. The prior national-security category therefore should be cleared or replaced only if the catalog supports a biographical category.
notes: The source does not establish an exact July 1, 1964 enrollment date or the sister-homework allegation. This is biographical context, not a documented public-policy or harm event.

evidence_resolution.proposed_title: Donald Trump Attended Fordham for Two Years Before Transferring to Penn
evidence_resolution.proposed_claim: Donald Trump attended Fordham for two years, appears as a freshman and squash-team member in the 1965 yearbook, and later transferred to the University of Pennsylvania; the precise enrollment day and homework allegation are unsupported.

supported_facts: The report says Trump attended Fordham for two years before transferring to Penn.
The report cites the 1965 yearbook and alumni interviews for his freshman-year squash-team participation.
limitations: The source does not establish an exact July 1, 1964 enrollment date or the sister-homework allegation. This is biographical context, not a documented public-policy or harm event.

title: TrumpFile Reports an Unverified Transcript Alleging Mogilevich–Putin Contacts
description_short: TrumpFile published an excerpt attributed to a 2000 Kuchma–Derkach conversation; its recording is unauthenticated, and no Trump connection is shown.
description_medium: TrumpFile presents an excerpt it attributes to a private conversation between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and former security chief Leonid Derkach, reportedly recorded by Mykola Melnychenko. Derkach is quoted as saying Semion Mogilevich had longstanding contact with Vladimir Putin. The page says the transcript’s authenticity was not independently verified and supplies no Donald Trump connection.
description_long: The supportable event is the publication of a TrumpFile timeline entry, not a verified recording or a Trump-related event. The page says that an excerpt dated February 8, 2000, came from a private conversation between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and Leonid Derkach, then head of Ukraine’s security service, and identifies Mykola Melnychenko as the person who recorded it. In the excerpt, Kuchma asks about Semion Mogilevich; Derkach is quoted as saying Mogilevich was on good terms with Vladimir Putin and had been in contact with Putin since his Leningrad period. TrumpFile attributes the transcript to journalist J. V. Koshiw’s published work. The page itself cautions that the recording’s authenticity had not been independently verified. The packet provides no authenticated recording or independent transcript confirmation, and the excerpt does not mention Donald Trump. Accordingly, the title and description attribute the reported statement rather than assert it as fact. This material does not substantiate the original Trump-framed claim or its prior human-rights/immigration classification.
notes: The source does not independently authenticate the recording or transcript. The quoted statement is an allegation within attributed dialogue, not verified fact; no connection to Trump appears.

evidence_resolution.proposed_title: TrumpFile Reports an Unverified Transcript Alleging Mogilevich–Putin Contacts
evidence_resolution.proposed_claim: TrumpFile published an excerpt it attributes to an unauthenticated 2000 Kuchma–Derkach conversation, in which Derkach reportedly described contacts between Mogilevich and Putin; the excerpt does not connect to Donald Trump.

supported_facts: The TrumpFile page was published as a timeline item dated February 8, 2000 and includes an excerpt attributed to Kuchma and Derkach.
The excerpt attributes to Derkach the claim that Mogilevich had longstanding contact with Putin.
limitations: The source does not independently authenticate the recording or transcript. The quoted statement is an allegation within attributed dialogue, not verified fact; no connection to Trump appears.

title: Reports Place Rybolovlev’s Jet Near Two 2016 Trump Campaign Stops
description_short: Flight-record reporting placed Rybolovlev’s jet near two Trump campaign stops in 2016; it does not establish that the men met or traveled together.
description_medium: A Philadelphia Inquirer report citing McClatchy flight records said Dmitry Rybolovlev’s aircraft landed in Las Vegas on October 30, 2016, when Trump held a rally there, and in Charlotte on November 3, near another campaign stop. The plane reached Charlotte less than an hour after Trump’s campaign aircraft. Rybolovlev’s representative denied contact. These movements do not prove the men met.
description_long: The Philadelphia Inquirer reported on flight records obtained by McClatchy that showed two airport overlaps between aircraft associated with Dmitry Rybolovlev and Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign. On October 30, Rybolovlev’s plane landed in Las Vegas on the day Trump campaigned there; the report said the jet spent about an hour and 20 minutes on the ground and taxied to a private hangar used by casino owner Sheldon Adelson. On November 3, Rybolovlev’s aircraft arrived at Charlotte Douglas International Airport less than an hour after Trump’s campaign plane, while Trump appeared at a rally in nearby Concord. Rybolovlev’s representative said the trip was for business and that he had no contact with Trump or his advisers. The reported records document aircraft movements and the representative’s denial. They do not establish that either man was aboard at the same time, that the two men met or communicated, or that the travel was coordinated. The original wording “cross paths” overstates what the evidence establishes; this draft keeps the claim at aircraft proximity.
notes: Aircraft locations do not prove passenger identity, simultaneous presence of the men, a meeting, communication, or coordination. The Inquirer attributes flight-record information to McClatchy.

evidence_resolution.proposed_title: Reports Place Rybolovlev’s Jet Near Two 2016 Trump Campaign Stops
evidence_resolution.proposed_claim: Flight-record reporting described Rybolovlev’s aircraft at Las Vegas and Charlotte around two Trump campaign stops in October and November 2016; the men’s presence together or contact was not established.

sources.title: “Russian billionaire says it was ‘pure coincidence’ his jet shadowed Trump’s” — The Philadelphia Inquirer

supported_facts: The report places Rybolovlev’s aircraft in Las Vegas on October 30, 2016, the date of a Trump campaign rally.
The report places Rybolovlev’s aircraft in Charlotte less than an hour after Trump’s campaign plane on November 3, 2016.
Rybolovlev’s representative said the trip was for business and denied contact with Trump or his advisers.
limitations: Aircraft locations do not prove passenger identity, simultaneous presence of the men, a meeting, communication, or coordination. The Inquirer attributes flight-record information to McClatchy.

title: Trump Media Merger Closed in March 2024; Trump Reported 78.75 Million Shares
description_short: Trump Media’s merger closed March 25, 2024; Trump’s SEC filing reported 78.75 million shares, about 57.6% of the outstanding stock at that time.
description_medium: An SEC filing says Digital World Acquisition Corp.’s merger with Trump Media & Technology Group closed March 25, 2024, after shareholders approved it on March 22. Donald Trump’s April 1 Schedule 13D reported beneficial ownership of 78.75 million shares, about 57.6% of shares then outstanding. These filings establish the transaction and reported ownership, not the packet’s $3–4 billion valuation or allegations of manipulation.
description_long: Digital World Acquisition Corp. and Trump Media & Technology Group completed their business combination on March 25, 2024, according to Digital World’s Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing says shareholders approved the transaction at a special meeting on March 22 and that the public company adopted the Trump Media & Technology Group name at closing. Donald Trump’s Schedule 13D, filed April 1, reported beneficial ownership of 78,750,000 shares, approximately 57.6 percent of the shares outstanding on March 25. These filings establish the merger date and Trump’s reported share count and percentage. The source originally attached to this timeline entry is a Reuters article about Trump’s New York hush-money trial and does not support the merger claim. The supplied packet’s $3–4 billion figure is a market-value estimate that requires a specified date and share price; these filings do not substantiate that number as proceeds received. The records also do not establish market manipulation, insider enrichment, or other wrongdoing. The narrower draft describes the corporate transaction and disclosed ownership only, with no financial-misconduct conclusion.
notes: The original Reuters URL concerns the hush-money trial and is unrelated. No share-price date or valuation calculation supports the $3–4 billion estimate as stated; share value is not realized proceeds. No evidence of manipulation or insider enrichment is provided.

evidence_resolution.proposed_claim: The Trump Media–Digital World merger closed March 25, 2024; Trump’s SEC filing reported 78.75 million shares, approximately 57.6% of outstanding shares at closing.

title: Clemency Claim Involving White House Remains Unresolved Without Article Details
description_short: A Sentinel headline attributes a clemency-involvement claim to Rep. Peters, but the unavailable article and packet omit the recipient, action, evidence, and outcome.
description_medium: The supplied Grand Junction Sentinel headline says Rep. Peters claimed the White House was involved in a clemency matter and mentions officials’ reactions to social-media posts and an agency call. The article body was unavailable in the prior review. The packet does not identify Peters, the recipient, the clemency decision, the posts, or the agency. The headline alone cannot verify the claim.
description_long: The available evidence is limited to the title and URL of a Grand Junction Sentinel article. Its headline attributes to “Peters” a statement that the White House was involved in clemency and references officials reacting to social-media posts and an agency call. The article body was inaccessible during the source review, and the packet supplies no publication date, full name or role for Peters, named clemency recipient, description of the decision, text of the posts, agency involved, or documentary evidence behind the allegation. It is therefore possible to report only that the headline attributed an allegation; the alleged White House role cannot be presented as established fact. A supportable event narrative requires the complete article or an archived copy, the identity and statement of the relevant representative, the recipient and clemency action, and any records that clarify what White House or agency officials did. Until then, retain an unresolved proposal rather than publish a factual account of political favoritism or intervention.
notes: The source body, date, Peters’s identity, clemency recipient and decision, referenced posts, agency, supporting evidence, and outcome are missing. The allegation is not established.

evidence_resolution.proposed_title: Clemency Claim Involving White House Remains Unresolved Without Article Details

title: No DOJ Roster Match Verifies a Trump Commutation for Tanya Santos
description_short: The cited DOJ roster has no Tanya Santos match, and no clemency instrument or case details in the packet verify that Trump commuted her sentence.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s roster of commutations granted by President Trump from 2017 through 2021 contains no Tanya Santos match in the focused review. The packet provides no court, conviction, sentence, signed commutation, or alternate recipient name. The claim cannot be verified from the linked source. Keep it out of a confirmed clemency chronology until an identifiable primary record is located.
description_long: The linked Justice Department page is a roster of commutations granted by President Donald Trump from 2017 through 2021. The focused review found no entry for Tanya Santos. The packet provides no court or case number, conviction, sentence, signed commutation, date of clemency, or alternate name that could identify a matching recipient. The evidence therefore supports a narrow statement about the lookup result: this roster does not verify the claimed commutation under the supplied name. It does not establish that no commutation occurred under another spelling or identity, so the absence of a match should not be overstated as proof of nonoccurrence. To resolve the entry, a clemency warrant or order, a DOJ recipient record under an identifiable name, or case documentation linking Tanya Santos to a different recorded recipient is needed. Until then, the event should remain unresolved and excluded from any list of verified Trump clemency actions. The original classification alleging corrupt pardons is unsupported by the available evidence and should be cleared.
notes: A roster miss does not rule out an alternate spelling or identity. No clemency instrument, alternate name, court, case number, conviction, or sentence is supplied. The corrupt-pardon classification has no supporting evidence.

evidence_resolution.proposed_claim: The cited DOJ commutations roster contains no Tanya Santos match, and the packet supplies no primary clemency document or case identity to verify the reported commutation.
